page: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server utilizing the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 9575F processor with an x86_64 architecture, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The CPU configuration consists of 16 physical cores with a 1.0 thread-per-core ratio, allocated on a shared basis. The system is equipped with 192.0 GB of system memory, providing 12.0 GB of RAM per core. For acceleration, it includes two NVIDIA L40S GPUs based on the Ada Lovelace architecture, delivering a combined total of 96 GB of VRAM. No local storage is bundled with this instance.

Benchmark data indicates top-tier single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression all ranking in the top 10%. Multi-core CPU performance, including Geekbench multi-core and stress-ng multi-core, falls into the top 25%. Large block memory bandwidth read and write operations also rank in the top 25%, though small block cached read bandwidth is average. Large language model inference speeds for a small 135M model reach the top 10% for both prompt processing and text generation, while performance scales to the top 25% for medium 7B model text generation and average for large 70B models.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the server offers high resource density by pairing a substantial 192.0 GB memory footprint with dual enterprise-grade L40S GPUs, though the shared CPU allocation represents a potential tradeoff for workloads requiring sustained, dedicated CPU performance. The absence of local storage requires external storage provisioning. This configuration is engineered for workloads such as machine learning inference, data science, image processing, and parallelized compute tasks that leverage GPU acceleration and high memory capacity.
description: UpCloud GPU-16xCPU-192GB-2xL40S is a GPU-accelerated server featuring 16 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9575F processor, 192.0 GB of system memory, and two NVIDIA L40S GPUs with 96 GB of total VRAM. Built on the x86_64 architecture under the KVM hypervisor, this instance does not include local storage. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core CPU performance and strong multi-core capabilities, ranking in the top 10% for single-threaded compression and small-model LLM inference. Large block memory bandwidth and multi-core Geekbench scores place in the top 25%. While the shared CPU allocation and lack of local storage are notable tradeoffs, the high memory-to-core ratio and dual GPUs make this server suitable for machine learning inference, image processing, and data science workloads.
